page: Amazon Web Services c9g.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system provides two dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. It features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, giving an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, and baseline networking throughput is rated at 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant single-threaded efficiency on the ARMv9 cores. In single-core tests, the c9g.large achieves top-tier results in Geekbench (2306.0), gzip compression (36.49 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (17.21 GB/sec). However, the absolute multi-core capacity remains bounded by the two-core hardware limit, placing stress-ng multi-core (4001.26) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (34.0 GB/sec) in lower percentiles. Cryptographic operations also show low scores, with PassMark encryption reporting 593.68.

Because of its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance prioritizes raw per-core execution efficiency over memory capacity. This configuration provides a cost-effective operational profile for single-threaded processing pipelines, light web serving throughput (8.17 GB/sec), and moderate in-memory key-value caching (6.48 million Redis SET operations per second). Workloads dependent on large working memory footprints, local NVMe storage, or complex multi-threaded concurrency will encounter hardware bottlenecks.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.large is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors running at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It features two dedicated physical cores, 4.0 GB of system RAM (2.0 GB per core), and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks show top-tier single-threaded compute efficiency, registering a 2306.0 Geekbench single-core score and 36.49 GB/sec gzip compression throughput. However, aggregate multi-threaded performance is constrained by its two-core profile, reflected in lower PassMark CPU and stress-ng multi-core metrics. Memory-intensive tasks are bounded by the 4.0 GB memory capacity. Overall, the hardware configuration suits single-threaded processing queues, lightweight static web servers, microservices, and general compute tasks that do not require extensive memory capacity or local disk storage.

4.0 GB system memory providing a compute-focused 1:2 core-to-memory ratio
Strong single-thread performance across compression and CPU benchmarks
Baseline 1 Gbps networking throughput running on the Nitro hypervisor
Requires attached remote storage due to lack of local disk volumes
Well-suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, and single-threaded batch jobs
